anomalies.observed: J4 pin 1 is labeled MISO and pin 4 is labeled MOSI, but these nets do not connect to the ATtiny devices: U2/U3 PB0 is labeled SDA and PB1 is labeled PWM.
anomalies.expected: For AVR ISP programming, J4 MISO should connect to the ATtiny PB1/MISO pin and J4 MOSI should connect to the ATtiny PB0/MOSI pin, sharing those nets with the normal SDA/PWM functions.

evidence.quote: J4 AVR-ISP-6: pin 1 MISO, pin 4 MOSI; U2 pin 5 PB0 labeled SDA, pin 6 PB1 labeled PWM; U3 pins 5 and 6 similarly SDA/PWM.

anomalies.impact: The AVR-ISP header cannot program the ATtiny because MISO and MOSI are left open; the board is effectively unprogrammable through its dedicated ISP connector.

anomalies.observed: R3, the 10 kΩ pull-up on the RESET net, has its top end connected to the VCC power symbol while the ATtiny supply pins are connected to +5V.
anomalies.expected: The RESET pull-up should connect to the ATtiny logic supply (+5V), not to the raw VCC input rail.

evidence.quote: R3 10K: top end to VCC, bottom end to RST; U2/U3 VCC pin 8 connected to +5V.

anomalies.impact: RESET is pulled toward the raw VCC rail (likely higher than 5 V) instead of the 5 V logic rail, potentially overstressing the ATtiny RESET pin and causing unreliable reset or programming behaviour.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains at least two real deviations: the AVR-ISP MISO/MOSI pins are not connected to the ATtiny, and the RESET pull-up R3 is tied to VCC instead of the +5V logic rail.
